subject: [URGENT] BridgePoint: cache burst causing silo starvation / immediate mitigation plan
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@bridgepoint.ai>
To: rohan.mehta@redwood.ai
Cc: sre@bridgepoint.ai
Date: Mon, 06 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: High tail latency and 5xx spike — possible cache thrash

Hi RoHan,

We started seeing a sharp jump in request p99 and a corresponding 500-rate spike on our production tenant around 08:50 PDT — coincides with a nightly analytics job. Latency p50 is fine but p95/p99 and error rate jumped quickly. Our dashboard shows a small set of prefixes (customer-docs/) hitting a single hot shard and a ton of KV cache evictions.

Attached: kv_stats_20280506.csv (KV hit/eviction timeline), slo_snapshot_0506.png

Can you confirm if any config change on your side or recent model patch could cause prefix affinity to concentrate? This is causing revenue-impacting errors for a handful of key customers. Please escalate — we need a mitigation plan within the hour.

Thanks,
Elena
Principal SRE, BridgePoint


From: rohan.mehta@redwood.ai <rohan.mehta@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@bridgepoint.ai>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 06 May 2028 09:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High tail latency and 5xx spike — possible cache thrash

Hi Elena — thanks for the alert and the attachments. I’m pulling the engineering response team in now.

Quick notes from initial triage:
- We don’t have any deployment to BridgePoint in the last 24 hours; no model binary/weights change rolled.
- There was an autoscaler bump in host capacity at ~08:45 (background scaling activity) but that should *reduce* head-of-line issues, not create them.
- The KV stats file shows a burst of evictions exactly when p99 rises — suggests hot-key thrash and prefix mapping skew.

Immediate actions I’m requesting from engineering: can we do an emergency soft-fallback routing to the compatible model variant with larger KV quota for the affected tenant? If we can’t shift traffic, can we temporarily increase the KV cache allocation for BridgePoint’s tenant to absorb the burst?

Marissa / Ben — can you confirm feasibility and ETA on a config-side fix (routing override or KV bump)? If not possible in 30–45m, I’ll escalate to Ops to enforce admission control (rate limit) for the offending prefixes to protect overall cluster SLOs.

I’ll keep you posted.
-Rohan
Account Exec — Redwood Inference

From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: rohan.mehta@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 06 May 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High tail latency and 5xx spike — possible cache thrash

RoHan / Ben — quick sync notes from ops triage (10:00):
* Root cause hypothesis:* periodic nightly batch (analytics indexing) emits large prefix-scoped calls (avg seq_len 2k tokens) that map to a small subset of KV shards due to our current prefix->shard hashing and short-lived prefix caching TTL. That combination causes: continuous eviction of cold keys, KV hot shard queuing, and then head-of-line blocking for dependent requests.

*Evidence:* 
- KV eviction spike correlates exactly with BridgePoint job window in kv_stats_20280506.csv.
- Heap pressure on those worker processes increased; we captured a small heap snapshot (heap_snapshot_stub.txt) indicating heavy KV entry churn.
- Batching metric shows sudden increase in batch sizes for hot lane (from 16->72), which is making sequence processing slower and exacerbating HOL delays.

*Fast mitigations (actionable now):*
1) Routing override to shift 20% of BridgePoint traffic to a compatible variant with 2x KV quota and larger per-shard memory — takes ~12 minutes to enable via admin route.
2) Increase per-tenant KV quota for BridgePoint by 3x for the next 2 hours — config change, avoids routing churn; ~7–10 minutes to apply.
3) If neither is feasible, apply temporary prefix admission control (rate limit) for the analytics job prefixes — blocks the burst and protects overall SLOs; immediate (~3 minutes) but customer-visible errors for those jobs.

I recommend option 2 first (KV quota bump) since it’s lowest customer impact. Ben — please stage the change now and we’ll execute on my mark once we have exec signoff.

Jonas — flagging this for possible exec attention if the customer pushes; they’re requesting <1h mitigation.

-Marissa
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: rohan.mehta@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 06 May 2028 17:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High tail latency and 5xx spike — possible cache thrash

Thanks team — quick executive decision record: we authorized the temporary KV quota increase (option 2) for BridgePoint for a 2-hour window. Ben executed the change at 10:14 PDT and we observed p99 drop by ~320ms and 5xx rate return to baseline within 9 minutes.

Follow-ups assigned:
- Marissa: run a deeper postmortem on prefix->shard hashing and propose a durable mitigation (possible approaches: hash diversification, per-prefix jittered TTLs, or adaptive hot-shard split). Due EOD tomorrow.
- Ben: capture a reproducible load test that triggers the eviction pattern and add a derivation to RED-8421. Include runbook steps for emergency KV bump and routing override.
- RoHan: keep BridgePoint engaged; offer a credits package for the hour of degraded SLA and coordinate CS ticket for billing/compensation.

Jonas Weber
VP, Production Reliability
Redwood Inference

P.S. Elena — our CS rep will follow up on compensation. Apologies for the impact; we’ll share the postmortem and permanent fixes ASAP.
